title: Predicting Intraday Trading Volume with News Sentiment: An Analysis of U.S. Airline Stocks

detail.title: Predicting Intraday Trading Volume with News Sentiment: An Analysis of U.S. Airline Stocks
detail.abstract: When institutional traders buy or sell large amounts of stock, they often have to consider the impact of their trades on the market price. Existing literature has shown that trading volume can be reliably forecasted and can translate to reduced price impact on large trades. In this paper, we attempt to model 15-minute ahead trading volume for 7 U.S. airline stocks with a large set of financial variables as well as sentiment measures from the Global Database of Events, Language, and Tone (GDELT). Through a combination of feature engineering, model selection, and hyperparameter tuning, we achieve an out-of-sample R^2 of just over 70% in the prediction of 15-minute-ahead trading volume, over a testing period of approximately 18 months. Our best model explains 15 percentage points more variation than a naive forecast, and is comparable with state-of-the-art models in the literature. We find that sentiment measures improve the model's predictions, but only marginally so. These results suggest that sentiment measures are not necessary for accurate trading volume prediction, but they do not hurt the model's performance either.

title: Risk Choice and Voluntary Disclosure
affiliations: San Diego State University - Finance Department and Sungkyunkwan University, SKK GSB

detail.title: Risk Choice and Voluntary Disclosure
detail.abstract: This paper presents a model in which investors price risk and a firm makes an investment to reduce its cash flow risk. Subsequently, the firm may or may not privately receive information about the future cash flow, whose disclosure is under its discretion. We show that the equilibrium cash flow precision increases with investor risk aversion, but decreases with the likelihood that the firm has private information and the quality of that information. In addition, the equilibrium probability of disclosure increases when the firm is more likely to have higher-quality private information, but it may increase or decrease when investor risk aversion increases. Using these comparative statics, we rationalize mixed empirical findings on the relation between risk and disclosure as equilibrium outcomes. The model is extended to a setting where the firm also makes an investment to increase the mean of its future cash flow.

title: Do Workplace Pregnancy Accommodations Affect Fertility and Infant Health? Evidence from the 2022 Pregnant Workers Fairness Act
affiliations: University of Wisconsin-Madison and University of Wisconsin-Madison

detail.title: Do Workplace Pregnancy Accommodations Affect Fertility and Infant Health? Evidence from the 2022 Pregnant Workers Fairness Act
detail.abstract: The 2022 federal Pregnant Workers Fairness Act mandates reasonable accommodationsfor pregnant workers. By increasing women’s earnings and income duringpregnancy and making work safer, the law has the potential to improve health duringpregnancy and reduce pregnancy losses, leading to more live births. Using syntheticdifference-in-differences and rapid release natality data, we find a 3.2 percent increasein births in states newly covered by the PWFA, implying a nearly 9.6 percent reductionin pregnancy loss. We use Google Trends and NIESS injury data to provideevidence of a first stage and to rule out anticipation effects. Estimates are robust toa range of specifications and bootstrapped and placebo inference. Results providelawmakers with novel evidence of a net reduction in pregnancy loss due to safer workconditions.

title: The Impact of Empowering Leadership on the Safety Behavior of Chinese Civil Aviation Pilots: The Roles of Basic Psychological Needs Satisfaction and Trait Mindfulness
affiliations: Shaanxi Normal University, Shaanxi Normal University, Shaanxi Normal University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Shaanxi Normal University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Shaanxi Normal University and Shaanxi Normal University

detail.title: The Impact of Empowering Leadership on the Safety Behavior of Chinese Civil Aviation Pilots: The Roles of Basic Psychological Needs Satisfaction and Trait Mindfulness
detail.abstract: The safety behavior of civil aviation pilots is central to ensuring flight safety. This study conducted a questionnaire survey of 432 civil aviation pilots from Tibet Airlines Co., Ltd., China, to explore the impact of empowering leadership on pilots’ safety behavior, as well as the roles of basic psychological needs and trait mindfulness. After controlling for age, rank, and flight experience duration, the results showed: (1) empowering leadership positively predicts the safety behavior of civil aviation pilots; (2) empowering leadership influences pilots’ safety behavior indirectly through basic psychological needs satisfaction; (3)and the indirect effect of empowering leadership on pilots’ safety behavior is moderated by trait mindfulness: specifically, as trait mindfulness decreases, the predictive effect of basic psychological needs satisfaction on safety behavior increases. This study reveals the value of empowering leadership in enhancing civil aviation pilots’ safety behavior, providing new perspectives for promoting pilots’ mental health and safety behavior, as well as theoretical guidance and a practical basis for aviation safety management.
